role: NgRx effects class of a feature slice.

describedBy.text: File lives in `<area>/data-access/+state/`; class `<PascalCaseArea>Effects` with `@Injectable()` **without** `providedIn: 'root'`; registered through `provideEffects([...])` on the route; `/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/member-ordering */` at the top is allowed.

items.text: File lives in `<area>/data-access/+state/`; class `<PascalCaseArea>Effects` with `@Injectable()` **without** `providedIn: 'root'`; registered through `provideEffects([...])` on the route; `/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/member-ordering */` at the top is allowed.

Dependencies via `inject()` as `private readonly _camelCase`; the field name is the full descriptive name derived from the injected type (keeping the feature/area part of the class name), never shortened to a generic role name; the action stream is `_actions$ = inject(Actions)`; every effect field is camelCase with a `$` suffix.

Canonical HTTP effect: `ofType → <flattening operator of ngrx-effects#7> → service call → map(success) / catchError(fail)`; `catchError` sits **inside** the flattening operator and returns `of(failAction)` — outside it kills the stream after the first error.

The success/failure split may be written as `mapResponse({ next, error })` from `@ngrx/operators` instead of `map` + `catchError`: one operator, both branches returning actions, and no way to leave the error handling outside the flattening operator by accident. Both forms are accepted — and a `mapResponse` whose `error` branch returns nothing breaks the rule below exactly like a `catchError` that does.

The error path never ends in `EMPTY`: `catchError` returns `of(failAction)`. An effect whose error branch returns `EMPTY`/`NEVER` (or only a `tap`) swallows the failure — the reducer never receives a fail action, so `loading` stays `true`, the spinner never stops and the user is told nothing; report from that consequence (🔴 High). Outside effects `EMPTY` is legitimate (legacy components/services deliberately completing a stream) and is not reported there.

The error path opens no toast/snackbar/alert on its own: the failure reaches the user through the state the fail action writes and the template renders. A notification is correct only where the mockups or the requirements explicitly ask for one — a `tap` firing it from `catchError` without that basis is a finding, as is a second notification next to the one a shared error interceptor already shows.

Flattening operator by what the request does: `switchMap` ONLY for a read whose older answer is worthless once a newer one is asked for (a search, a reload of a list); a command - anything that writes, starts or changes something (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, a load, an unload, a label operation) - uses `mergeMap` when operations on different entities may run side by side, `concatMap` when their order matters, `exhaustMap` to ignore repeats until the first one completes. `switchMap` on a command cancels the in-flight request when the next action of its type arrives, and the first operation's success or failure never reaches the store or the user.
State lookups use `concatLatestFrom` from `@ngrx/operators` (never `withLatestFrom`); it may take an array of selectors and may call a payload-parameterized selector.

An effect that dispatches nothing declares `{ dispatch: false }` as the second `createEffect` argument. Without it NgRx dispatches whatever the stream emits — and when that value is (or triggers) an action the effect's own `ofType` listens to, every emission re-triggers the effect: an infinite dispatch loop (report from this consequence, as High).

`tap` is only for side effects (closing dialogs, events, notifying shared services, a notification the mockups or requirements ask for) and never changes stream data; related side effects share one `tap`; branching that picks the resulting action happens in `map`, with every branch returning an explicit action.
Effects triggered by cross-area/layout actions start with a `filter(...)` narrowing to their own area/step — otherwise every sibling area reacts to foreign events.
A `filter` after `concatLatestFrom` guards on state; when `0` is a valid value the check is an explicit `=== 0`/`!== null`, not truthiness.
Polling: an outer `switchMap` over `timer(0, <interval from the central app config>)` with an inner `switchMap` for the request; the interval is never hard-coded.
Polling: the inner pipe is closed with `takeUntil(this._stop$)`, where `_stop$` is a `private readonly Subject<void>`.
Polling: a separate `{ dispatch: false }` effect calls `_stop$.next()` on BOTH the stop and the fail actions — a fail that leaves the timer running polls a broken endpoint forever.
Multiple resulting actions are returned as an action array from one effect (branches unified with `of(action)` vs `[a, b]`) — not via `forkJoin` or duplicated effects.
Identical reactions to several actions are merged into one `ofType(a, b, c)`; the source is distinguished with `action.type === x.type` or `'prop' in action` type-narrowing.

Dialogs: `dialog.open<Component, Data, Result>(...)` always with all three generics; `afterClosed()` inside `switchMap`; cancellation is rejected with `filter((result): result is T => !!result)` before `map` (the predicate also removes the union with `null`/`false` without casting).
Bridging a dialog's outputs into actions may `merge(...)` the `afterClosed()` mapping with component-output streams, each guarded by `takeUntil(dialogRef.afterClosed())`.

An effect keeps its own logic: mapping a response, building a payload or branching inside the pipe does NOT have to become a `shared/utils/` function. Extraction is expected only for a second consumer or for a long (~10+ lines), genuinely complex body — never report "extract this into a util" for short single-consumer logic.

Pure composition helpers (type guards, response mapping, chain building) are module-level functions below the class; a private method is used only when it calls injected services; feature-flag branching is a `filter` in the pipe, not an `if` in `map`.

Forbidden: injecting a facade, `store.dispatch(...)` inside an effect (new actions are returned), manual `subscribe()`, mutating action payloads, a global `catchError`, domain logic inside `tap`, `Date.now()`/`Math.random()` in success payloads.

items.text:
No user-facing text is hard-coded in code or templates: every label, message, heading, tooltip and option text a user sees is a key of the base file, rendered through the translate pipe or resolved through the translation service — a `'Blocked'` returned by a mapper or a `

Users

` in a template is a finding, and so is a text an existing key already carries.

A value interpolated into text a user reads - a translate parameter (`{ slot, barcode }`), a template interpolation, a string concatenation, a copied or exported message - that can be `null` or `undefined` has an explicit fallback (`?? ''`, `?? '—'`) or a message variant without it: ngx-translate renders a missing parameter as the raw `{{slot}}` placeholder, and a template or a concatenation renders the word `null`.

Every feature area keeps the canonical layout: `data-access/+state/` (the view's `<name>.store.ts` signal store and, only for data several independent views share, an NgRx slice - actions, reducer, selectors, effects, facade - each with `tests/`), `data-access/services/` (HTTP only), `models/{consts,enums,interfaces,types}` with an `index.ts` barrel, `shared/{utils,guards,pipes,directives[,routes]}` each with `tests/`, plus `shared/mocks/` for the spec fixtures several specs share, `components-<area>/{feature,ui}/`, and for multi-step wizards a `shell/<area>-shell.routes.ts`. HTTP interceptors are app-level, never inside an area.
items.secondQuestion: Który element kanonicznego układu obszaru mieści ten plik i czy obszar ma ten element podwójnie albo poza układem (np. trasy i w `shared/routes/`, i w `shell/`)?

items.text: Facade and effects classes are `@Injectable()` **without** `providedIn: 'root'` - each route gets a fresh instance and fresh state; a `signalStore()` is never `{ providedIn: 'root' }` either - state that must outlive its view or be shared by several views is an NgRx slice.

Layering is strict: components touch state only through their view's signal store or, for data several views share, a facade - other services may be injected beside it, an HTTP service never; derived values are computed in the store (`withComputed` in a signal store, selectors in an NgRx slice); signal-store methods and effects orchestrate side effects and are the only consumers of HTTP services; HTTP services only perform requests.

Every file lives in its dedicated location: types/enums/consts in `models/`, pure functions in `shared/utils/`, guards in `shared/guards/`, pipes in `shared/pipes/`, directives in `shared/directives/`, spec fixtures several specs share in `shared/mocks/`, HTTP in `data-access/services/`, state files - the signal store and an NgRx slice's files - in `data-access/+state/`; next to a component file only `*.component.*` files and a `tests/` folder are allowed. A type, interface, enum or const used only inside its own file may stay there, without `export`; once it is exported or a second file needs it, it moves to `models/`. Spec fixtures and mocks several specs share are `<name>.mock.ts` files in the area's `shared/mocks/` - never a `*.fixtures.ts` file, and never under the `tests/` folder of a util or another layer.

Reuse before creating: nothing new (component, native-element markup, util, function, model, mapper, const, i18n key) is written before the shared library and the application have been SEARCHED for an equivalent — it usually already exists. The search is part of the change, not an optional courtesy: a hand-written table, input, button, dialog, tooltip or pagination, a util re-implementing a shared builder or ID generator, a second const/i18n key for a value already named somewhere — each is a finding that names the existing symbol to use instead. Only when the search genuinely comes back empty is a new element created, and then in the shared place its consumers can reach. A function shorter than 5 lines whose logic is simple - a single filter, map, find, some/every or sort over its input, or a property pick - is no such element: it is never reported for not reusing, or not becoming, a shared util.

An NgRx store slice (`createActionGroup`, `createReducer`, selectors, effects, a facade) exists only for data that several INDEPENDENT views read or write - different pages or routes, not the steps, children or dialogs of one view. A new slice, or a new action, state field or selector added to one, whose data only one view uses is a finding: that state belongs in the view's signal store. Data a second, independent view starts using moves into, or stays in, the NgRx slice.

Names are full and descriptive — no abbreviations and no one-letter identifiers; shortening is allowed only for well-established abbreviations or when the full name would exceed ~25–30 characters or 4–5 words.

items.text: A rename is complete: every name the change renames - a file or folder, an exported symbol, a class or store member, an input or output, a component/directive selector or pipe name, an action, a selector, a route path, a CSS class, a `data-test` value, an enum member, a translation key - has no use of its old name left anywhere in the repository: code, templates, styles, specs, mocks, snapshots, e2e tests, routes, barrels, configs and the base-language translation file (`en.json`), where a renamed key is renamed as well. The other locale files are the one exception: they are never touched (i18n#1), so the old key path they keep is no leftover. Whoever renames dispatches a fresh verification sub-agent once the rename is written (Agent tool, `general-purpose`): its prompt lists every old and new name and the repository root; it searches the whole tree but the other locale files for every old name - whole words, string literals, dotted translation-key paths and the key's leaf inside the nested `en.json` - and replies with each leftover `path:line`; every leftover is fixed and the sub-agent runs again until it finds none (a session without the Agent tool makes the same search itself and says so). A review judges the result only: an old name still in use is a finding at the renamed line, naming every leftover `path:line`.

A boolean - a field, signal, input, variable or a method returning a flag - is named with a predicate prefix that reads as a yes/no question (`isActive`, `hasChildren`, `canEdit`, `shouldRetry`; loading flags `isLoading<X>`), never a bare noun or adjective (`active`, `loading`, `children`). The fields of an API interface keep the names the API sends.

items.text: A comment explains only what the code cannot say itself - a non-obvious why, a tricky edge case, a workaround, a subtle gotcha; a comment restating what the code does or narrating obvious steps is a finding, and a clearer name replaces it. The section comments of a models barrel and the justification of a suppression comment are required, not this item's.

A long method is split into small, focused private helpers of the same file, each named after its one job; the split never creates a shared util or a new file for single-consumer logic (the utils instruction decides extraction).
One import declaration per module specifier: two `import` statements from the same path (`../../../models` twice) are merged into one.

instructions.name: Angular & TypeScript best practices
preamble: This instruction OWNS the framework-level API rules: typing, the signals API, DI, standalone declarables, host bindings, lazy routes, the forms pattern and RxJS usage. File placement and template rules belong to the component and component-template instructions; rendering cost and change detection to the performance instruction; WCAG 2.2 level AA — which new or changed UI must satisfy — to the accessibility instruction, which owns every accessibility finding. A violation is reported ONCE, under the most specific instruction covering it.

items.text: Strict typing everywhere: no `any` (use `unknown` plus narrowing when the shape is genuinely uncertain); prefer inference where the type is obvious; exported functions and service methods declare their parameter and return types. A signal input or output carries a type argument only when its default cannot express the type - `input.required<T>()`, `output<T>()`, `input<Item[]>([])`, `input<string | null>(null)` - never one its default already infers (`input(0)`, `input(false)`, `signal('')`, not `input<number>(0)`).

probe.message: argument typu powtarza typ, który wartość domyślna już wyznacza

items.text: Type annotations earn their place: annotate where inference is absent or wrong — an empty literal (`const items: Item[] = []`, `signal<Item[]>([])`), a `null`/`undefined` seed, an object literal assembled field-by-field against a domain interface, and the parameters plus return type of every exported function, service method and util. Never annotate what the call already types (`inject()`, `input(<default>)`, `signal()`/`computed()`/`toSignal()`, `_fb.nonNullable.group(...)`, `createSelector(...)`, `as const`, any variable initialized from a typed call) — a redundant annotation is boilerplate under the code-quality instruction. A view-model object a component or mapper builds for the template with fields of its own (a row extended with a tooltip, a disabled reason, a label) is typed by a named interface in `models/`, never left as an inferred object literal nobody declared.
No `subscribe()` inside a `subscribe()` — compose with `switchMap`/`concatMap`/`mergeMap`; the nested form leaks the inner subscription past every teardown operator on the outer one.

A suppression comment added by the diff (`@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `eslint-disable*`) carries a one-line justification and the narrowest scope that works (line-level over file-level); `@ts-expect-error` is used wherever it compiles, because it fails once the underlying problem is fixed. The `/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/member-ordering */` allowed by the effects instruction is the one standing exception.

Dependencies are injected with `inject()` - in a field initializer, a store's `withProps`/`withMethods`, or the body of a functional guard, resolver or interceptor - never through constructor parameters.
subject: constructor\s*\(

items.text: RxJS operators and creation functions are imported from `'rxjs'` - never from the deprecated `'rxjs/operators'` entry point, however much legacy code still imports it.
subject: rxjs/operators

items.text: A dialog, bottom sheet or overlay opened from an effect, a facade, a root service or any class whose injector is not the calling component's (`MatDialog.open`, `Dialog.open`, `Overlay.create`) passes `injector: <the caller's Injector>` whenever the opened component injects a route- or component-scoped provider (a feature facade, a signal store from `providers`): without it the dialog resolves from the root injector and throws NullInjectorError the moment it opens.

A value whose type allows `null` or `undefined` (an optional API field, a `string | null` message) that goes into user-facing text - a translation parameter, a toast or notification message, an interpolation - gets a fallback (`message ?? ''`) or a guard: otherwise the user reads the literal "null" or "undefined".

instructions.name: Performance & change detection
instructions.gate: the file holds Angular runtime code or a template - a component, directive, pipe, service, effect, store, config or bindings, not only type/const declarations or re-exports

items.text: Long-lived async work is bounded: polling/intervals take their period from the central app config and are explicitly stopped — no unbounded `setInterval`/`timer` outliving its view or effect.
items.subject: setinterval|interval|timer|poll|repeat|retry

instructions.name: Code quality — duplication, dead code, boilerplate & consistency
preamble: The two duplication items (the first two below) are reported with severity 🔴 **High**, every other violation of this checklist with 🟡 **Medium** — never softened because it looks cosmetic and never raised because it looks dangerous.

This instruction OWNS duplication, dead/unnecessary code, boilerplate and inconsistency: when another instruction or the cross-file pass covers the same occurrence (the architecture "reuse before creating" rule, the duplication-drift and naming-consistency questions, a jscpd candidate from the context), the occurrence is reported ONCE — here, with the severity above.

Scope is the skill's scope gate: the finding is anchored on a line the diff touched. A copy that the diff ADDS of pre-existing code is a finding (anchored on the new copy) once the code exists three or more times; duplication, dead code or inconsistency living entirely in untouched lines is not.

items.text: No duplicated logic: the same expression, condition, transformation, mapping, validator set, literal/const value or markup fragment appearing three or more times — in one file, across the files of this diff, or re-implemented next to an existing shared util, component, builder, model or i18n key, which counts as one of the copies (look for them with the Grep tool over the target's `snapshotDir`, the reviewed revision exported for this run, or with its `commands.grep` when it has none). Two occurrences are not a finding under this item. Test data a spec repeats in its own cases (fixture objects, the same literal in several cases) is unit-tests#12's, never this item's; logic a spec repeats stays here. Report every copy at the place that should reuse instead of repeat, and name the other copies. A function or expression shorter than 5 lines whose logic is simple - a single filter, map, find, some/every or sort over its input, or a property pick - is not duplicated logic under this item, however often it repeats: it is never reported as code to extract into a reusable util (utils#9).
items.secondQuestion: Które wyrażenia, pola, mapowania i literały tego pliku wyszukano w pozostałych plikach (stan, szablony, utils, modele, i18n) i z jakim wynikiem?

items.text: No copy-paste-with-a-tweak: three or more near-identical blocks differing only in a value, a field name or one branch become one parameterized function, const or loop — this includes near-identical test fixtures, mock objects and `it` bodies (which belong in an `it.each` dataset). Two such blocks are not a finding under this item.

items.text: No unused code: unused imports, variables, consts, parameters, private fields and methods, unreachable statements, dead branches, exported symbols with no consumer left in the repo, inputs/outputs nothing binds, and leftovers of an earlier iteration of this very change. This includes a public store, facade or service member (a field, a signal, a selector exposed through a facade, a method) that nothing in the repository reads, and a parameter every caller passes the same constant (`null`, `undefined`, `false`) - it is dropped, or given that value as its default.

No unnecessary code: a wrapper that only forwards to the wrapped call, a variable used once on the very next line, `else` after a `return`, a condition that can never be false, `?.`/`??`/`try` guarding a value the types already guarantee, a hand-written helper an existing shared function already provides, an abstraction (interface, base class, generic, options object) introduced for a single consumer "for the future".

No boilerplate: empty or pass-through lifecycle hooks and constructors, getters/methods that only return a field, scaffolding and generator leftovers (sample fields, `TODO` stubs nothing tracks), values re-declared although the framework already defaults to them, and ceremony that adds no behavior.

Code is consistent with its surroundings: one concept keeps one name everywhere (and one name never denotes two concepts), sibling cases are solved the same way (same guard style, same mapping approach, same error handling, same async style), related functions keep the same parameter order and return shape, and members keep the file's established ordering. Code that answers an already-answered question differently is a finding at the new location. A name that merely breaks a naming convention (casing, abbreviation) is not this rule — it is a finding only under the instruction that sets that convention. An inconsistency is a finding only when each variant is valid by itself; when a variant breaks another item, that item's finding is the one reported.

A property chain repeated three times or more in one function or test (`component.form.controls.x`, `fixture.componentInstance.y`) is destructured once at its top (`const { labelMethod, capacity } = component.form.controls;`).

instructions.name: Test coverage — untested cases & edge cases
instructions.gate: the file carries behaviour a spec could execute - a function or class method with a body (however trivial - a one-line setter or a lone .next() call is behaviour), a branch, handler or effect - not only declarations, re-exports or route/config literals
preamble: This instruction OWNS coverage gaps — which behavioral cases, branches, edge cases and state permutations the diff leaves untested; every finding here is 🔵 **Missing Unit Test**. The unit-tests instruction owns the SHAPE of a spec (location, setup, naming, assertion style). A gap is reported ONCE, here — never also as a unit-tests finding. The items below are facets of one requirement — the file's behaviour is tested — so everything a file breaks here is ONE finding: its Problem lists each untested case with its line, and its Reguła names every item it breaks. A file with no spec at all leaves its branches, failure paths and edge cases untested too: those items are broken, not passed, and that one finding names them.

items.text: Every new or behavior-changing source file in the diff ships the matching spec change in the same diff; a missing or untouched spec for changed behavior is a 🔵 Missing Unit Test finding. The file types their own instructions exempt are never such a finding: `models/` declarations, route files, i18n JSON, barrels, templates and styles — their behavior is covered by the specs of the code that consumes them.
Do not assume coverage from the spec's mere existence — enumerate the behavioral cases the changed lines introduce and cross-check each one against the spec's actual test cases.
items.okEvidence: linia każdego zmienionego zachowania i ścieżka spec z liniami przypadków, które je sprawdzają, nie zakres pliku

items.text: Every conditional branch introduced or modified by the diff is tested for BOTH outcomes: each `if`/`else`, ternary, `switch` case (including `default`), guard clause, early return and short-circuit path (`&&`, `||`, `??`, `?.`).
Every failure path is tested, not only the happy path: rejected promises, erroring observables/HTTP calls, thrown exceptions, `catch`/`catchError` blocks, timeout/retry logic and fallback values.

Edge cases of the data the changed code reads are covered: empty array/collection, `null`/`undefined` input, empty string, `0` and negative numbers, boundary values of every comparison (test the exact limit of `<` vs `<=`), first/last element handling, duplicates where uniqueness matters.

State permutations are covered: every boolean/loading/error flag the changed code reads is exercised in its non-default state as well as its default, and each flag is asserted independently so a single flag flipping the result is caught.
Public API surface changed by the diff (new method, new input/output, new selector/action handling) has at least one test exercising it through that public surface, not only through internals.
